title: Mirai_Worm_Investigation_8ed
description: Investigate a network compromised by a variant of the Mirai worm named Linux/Mirai.Y!tr.bdr. Identify the infection, understand its behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Mirai worm is a well-known malware that targets Linux-based IoT devices. It scans for devices using default credentials and exploits them to create a botnet. In this scenario, you will investigate a network compromised by a variant of the Mirai worm named Linux/Mirai.Y!tr.bdr. Your goal is to identify the infection, understand its behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the patient-zero host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the network and other compromised hosts.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the patient-zero host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the network and other compromised hosts.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious scheduled task/timer created by the malware
levels.content: The Mirai worm creates a scheduled task to maintain persistence. Investigate the systemd timers on the patient-zero host to find the suspicious timer.
levels.solution: The suspicious scheduled task/timer created by the malware is `sysnet-monitor.timer`. This timer is located in the `/etc/systemd/system/` directory and is used to maintain the persistence of the malware.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for timers in the `/etc/systemd/system/` directory.

levels.title: Identify the hidden malware directory
levels.content: The Mirai worm creates a hidden directory to store its files. Search the filesystem on the patient-zero host to find this directory.
levels.solution: The hidden malware directory created by the Mirai worm is `/opt/.worm`. This directory is used to store the malware's files and is typically hidden to avoid detection.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check directories that are not typically used by the system.

levels.title: Identify the beaconing mechanism used by the malware
levels.content: The Mirai worm communicates with a command and control (C2) server. Investigate the scripts in the hidden malware directory to find the beaconing mechanism.
levels.solution: The beaconing mechanism used by the malware is `/opt/.worm/beacon.sh`. This script is responsible for communicating with the command and control (C2) server and is located in the hidden malware directory.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for scripts that make network connections to the attacker host.
